summary: Pavel Trost was a linguist who studied at Masaryk University, the German University in Prague, Charles University under Friedrich Karl Slotty (Ph.D. 1934), and Palacký University. He held positions at Masaryk University, Palacký University, and Charles University (1956–1975).
Pavle Jevtić worked in Indology and philosophy. He was a disciple of Dimitrije Mitrinović and earned his Ph.D. from the SOAS University of London around 1924–1927.

Pavlo Grigorovič Ritter was an Indologist and linguist who studied at the University of Kharkiv under Dmitrij Nikolaevič Ovsjaniko-Kulikovskij and with Karl Friedrich Geldner. He became a professor at the University of Kharkiv in 1921, succeeding Ovsjaniko-Kulikovskij.

Pawan Goyal works in linguistics and Indology. He earned an M.Tech. from IIT Madras and a Ph.D. in mathematics from the Max Planck Institute for Dynamics of Complex Technical Systems (2018), later working at IIT Kharagpur (attested 2018–2025).

Pe Maung Tin was a scholar of Buddhist studies, linguistics, and Indology. He earned degrees from the universities of Rangoon, Calcutta, and Oxford. He served as professor of Pali and principal at the University of Rangoon (1937–1946).
Pedro Manuel Castro Sánchez is a scholar of Buddhist studies who earned an MA at the University of Sunderland, where he studied under Peter Harvey.

Pedro Roca y López was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Juan Gelabert y Gordiola and earned a Dr.phil. from Complutense University of Madrid. He held posts at the University of Barcelona (ca. 1880–1886) and National Library of Spain.

id: P:Pedro Urbano González de la Calle
summary: Pedro Urbano González de la Calle was a linguist and Indologist who earned his Ph.D. at Complutense University under Mario Daza de Campos. He held professorships at the universities of Valencia, Complutense, Barcelona, and later in Colombia and Mexico.

Pei-jung Wu is a scholar of history, archaeology, Japanology, and Buddhist studies. She earned a B.A. from National Taiwan University and completed a Ph.D. at UCLA in 2002 under doctoral supervisor Donald F. McCallum.

Pema Bhum is a Tibetologist who served as a professor of Tibetan languages and letters at Lanzhou University and Indiana University Bloomington. He also served as director of the Latse Contemporary Tibetan Cultural Library (attested 2003–2009).

Pema Chödrön is a Buddhist studies figure who studied at Sarah Lawrence College and UC Berkeley. She studied under teachers including Chögyam Trungpa, served as director of the Boulder Shambhala Center, and became director and abbess of Gampo Abbey.
Pema Donyo Nyinje is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology who studied under Kalu Rinpoche and Rangjung Rigpe Dorje. He has taught Ogyen Trinley Dorje and Yongey Mingyur Rinpoche.

Pema Gyaltsen is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under Khenpo Ngawang Pelzang and Khenchen Palden Sherab Rinpoche, and his students include Christopher S. George, Adam Pearcey, and Rizong Sras Rinpoche.
Pema Kunzang Tendzin studied under Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo and Jamgön Kongtrül Lodrö Thaye.
Pema Sherpa is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. She is a Ph.D. candidate in religious studies at McMaster University under the doctoral supervision of Shayne Clarke (attested 2026).
Pema Tekchok Loden studied under Shenphen Nangwa, Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo, Shechen Gyaltsab, and Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso.
Pema Tekchok Tenpai Gyeltsen studied under Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo, Jamgön Kongtrül Lodrö Thaye, and Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso. He taught Shenphen Nangwa, Khenpo Ngawang Pelzang, and Shechen Gyaltsab.
Pema Tsering is a Tibetologist who studied under Shenphen Nangwa and served as an editorial consultant at the University of Bonn (attested 1982).
Pema Vajra 01 studied under Shenphen Nangwa, Patrul Rinpoche, and Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso. He taught Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo, Shechen Gyaltsab, and Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso.
Pema Wangchok Gyelpo studied under Shenphen Nangwa, Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö, Khakyab Dorje, and Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso. He taught Shenphen Nangwa and Rangjung Rigpe Dorje.
